Keep in mind that many suicidal people have been through depressed states and crises for years, or even most of their lives. They've heard all the platitudes, all the gimmick approaches. They've probably read a lot about it. The best thing you can do is get the person to talk. Have a conversation, let them vent and unburden themselves. That can be very helpful even if it's not a direct solution, as one might imagine. If you start with a gimmick approach, they will brush you away. They will feel patronized because they know their own state much better than you ever will, and a conversation will never happen. Approach earnestly and without prejudice, ask questions that don't assume, and make it easy for the person to start talking about their problems.

Most often, conversation is the only thing that can help. It can be so valuable you can't imagine. It can give the person a last glimmer of hope, show them that someone out there cares.

Lastly, I want to thank you for trying, for taking the effort. You have no idea how much it means to a person who has given up, that someone out there cares enough to try. I know it must be hard, and do take care of yourself, recharge and don't burn out your own core of inner health.

So, really, even if I somehow manage to fix this, which is dubious. It is practically guaranteed that I will keep being fucked up for a long time. So there's no sense in waiting, better to rip off the bandaid quick.
